legend: Tissue fragments of markedly pleomorphic epithelioid and spindle malignant cells against a predominantly haemorrhagic background with degenerate cellular debris. (Giemsa)

Large epithelioid and pleomorphic cells with highly pleomorphic sometimes bizarre nuclei and variable eccentric cytoplasm containing fine vacuoles in some cells. Apoptosis and interspersed haemosiderophages are present in the haemorrhagic background. (Giemsa)
Spindle cells with elongated cytoplasm and more polygonal cells with round to oval nuclei from a moderately differentiated angiosarcoma. (Giemsa)
Low cellularity. Small and delicate malignant spindle cells against a  haemorrhagic background. Giemsa.
FISH shows multiple red signals of MYC (8q24) with one or two green signals of the control centromere of chromosome 8 (CEP8) in each tumour cell, indicative of amplification.
Haemorrhagic violaceous cutaneous lesion, lateral left breast.
Large tissue fragment consisting of spindle and some polygonal cells with nuclear pleomorphism showing a vasoformative pattern. (Giemsa)

legend: Metastatic to pleural fluid, showing pleomorphic epithelioid cells with high N:C ratios, large pleomorphic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and limited eccentric cytoplasm in minute tissue fragments and occasional single cells, in a background of contrasting bland macrophages and mesothelial cells to the right. (Pap)
Metastatic to pleural fluid, with large cells with one or more large nuclei, amid background histiocytes and a few mesothelial cells. (Giemsa)
Metastatic to pleural fluid showing a tissue fragment of epithelioid cells and a few dispersed mesothelial cells in a bloody background (Cell block; H&E)
Metastatic to pleural fluid, positive ICC for MYC in nuclei, characteristic of radiation-induced angiosarcoma. (Cell block)
The tumour cells stain for the vascular marker CD31, confirming the vascular derivation, while mesothelial cells do not stain. (IHC CD31)
Radiation-induced angiosarcoma of the breast, which subsequently metastasized to the pleura; slit-like spaces in subcutis and dermis. (Tissue section, H&E)

Cell block from blood clot. HE stain. Microscopically there are disrupted anastomosing blood vessels and a more solid vasoformative pattern with compressed and angulated lumina. The malignant endothelial cells reveal high grade atypia, confer nuclear size versus size of RBC. Histologically this was a primary angiosarcoma of the breast.   Same case as wsi #40686 and #40101 and #40104
